title: Semiconductor Process Foundations
description: From crystal to patterned films: wafer, oxidation, implant, deposition, etch, and why integration is later than any single step.

sourceReferences.title: MIT 6.152J Micro/Nano Processing Technology
sourceReferences.notes: Unit processes before a finished device. Lithography is one peer among oxidation, deposition, etch.

sourceReferences.title: MIT 6.774 Physics of Microfabrication
sourceReferences.notes: Front-end physics as mechanisms, not tool brochures.

modules.title: The wafer
modules.blurb: Crystal, cleanliness, and the starting surface.
learningObjectives: Treat cleanliness as yield before any pattern

modules.title: Adding and removing material
learningObjectives: Leave a surface flat enough for the next layer

modules.title: Making a device of it
modules.blurb: Isolation, gates, yield as a property of the flow.
learningObjectives: Read yield as a process property

concepts.name: Single-crystal silicon
concepts.summary: Why a chip starts as an ordered lattice, not a metal lump.
objectives: Explain why a chip starts as an ordered silicon lattice rather than a metal lump
Name what a grain boundary would do to a transistor that crosses it

concepts.name: Wafer preparation
concepts.summary: Slicing, polishing, and the surface everything else will inherit.
objectives: Trace slicing, lapping, and polish as the surface later films inherit
Say why the starting surface, not later magic, sets the first defect budget

concepts.name: Contamination and cleans
concepts.summary: Particles and metals as yield before any pattern exists.
objectives: Distinguish particles from metallic contamination
Explain why a clean happens before any pattern exists

concepts.name: Thermal oxidation
concepts.summary: Growing SiO2 from the wafer itself.
objectives: Contrast growing SiO2 from the wafer with depositing a film onto it
Predict how dry versus wet oxidation changes rate and film quality

concepts.name: Diffusion of dopants
concepts.summary: Concentration profiles as a function of time and temperature.
objectives: Describe a dopant profile as a function of time and temperature
Contrast a driven-in profile with a deposited surface source

concepts.name: Ion implantation
concepts.summary: Placing dopants with an accelerator, then repairing the damage.
objectives: Explain placing dopants with an accelerator rather than a furnace
Predict what lattice damage does if it is not later annealed

concepts.name: Anneal and activation
concepts.summary: Healing the lattice so the dopant actually dopes.
objectives: Explain why implanted dopant is not electrically active until the lattice heals
Name the thermal-budget trade-off an anneal spends

concepts.name: Chemical vapor deposition
concepts.summary: Growing a film from a gas that reacts on the surface.
objectives: Describe a film grown from a gas that reacts on the surface
Contrast conformal CVD coverage with line-of-sight arrival

concepts.name: Physical vapor deposition
concepts.summary: Throwing atoms at the wafer — sputtering and evaporation.
objectives: Describe sputtering or evaporation as throwing atoms at the wafer
Predict where a PVD film thins on a high-aspect sidewall

concepts.name: Epitaxy
concepts.summary: A film that continues the crystal underneath.
objectives: Define epitaxy as a film that continues the crystal underneath
Diagnose what a dirty or amorphous surface does to an epi layer

concepts.name: Wet etching
concepts.summary: Isotropic chemistry that undercuts.
objectives: Explain why wet chemistry undercuts a mask isotropically
Predict the remaining profile after a long wet etch

concepts.name: Plasma etching
concepts.summary: Anisotropic removal so sidewalls can be vertical.
objectives: Contrast anisotropic plasma etch with isotropic wet etch
Explain how ions and neutrals together make a vertical sidewall

concepts.name: Chemical-mechanical planarization
concepts.summary: Making the wafer flat enough for the next lithography.
objectives: Describe CMP as chemical plus mechanical removal that flattens
Predict what leftover topography does to the next exposure

concepts.name: Metallization
concepts.summary: Wires on the chip, and the barriers that keep them from wandering.
objectives: Explain why a barrier sits between a conductor and the dielectric
Name what happens if copper or aluminum wanders into silicon

concepts.name: Interlevel dielectrics
concepts.summary: The insulators between metal layers.
objectives: State the job of the insulator between metal layers
Contrast a deposited interlevel dielectric with a thermal gate oxide

concepts.name: Device isolation
concepts.summary: Keeping neighboring transistors from sharing a channel.
objectives: Explain how neighboring transistors are kept from sharing a channel
Contrast a field oxide or trench with just leaving more space

concepts.name: Wells and channel engineering
concepts.summary: The doped tubs a MOSFET lives in.
objectives: Describe a well as the doped tub a MOSFET sits in
Predict what a misplaced well dose does to threshold

concepts.name: The gate stack
concepts.summary: Dielectric plus electrode as the MOSFET's control surface.
objectives: Name the gate stack as dielectric plus electrode on the channel
Contrast a grown gate oxide with a deposited electrode

concepts.name: Silicides and contacts
concepts.summary: Low-resistance meetings of silicon and metal.
objectives: Explain a silicide as a low-resistance meeting of silicon and metal
Diagnose an open or leaky contact from a dirty interface or an overgrown spike

concepts.name: Process integration
concepts.summary: The sequence is the device. Order is not decorative.
objectives: State that the sequence of unit processes is the device
Predict a failure when a later high-temperature step wrecks an earlier profile

concepts.name: Yield as a process property
concepts.summary: Good die per wafer, owned by defectivity and process window.
objectives: Treat yield as good die per wafer, owned by defects and process window
Separate a killer defect from a parametric miss

concepts.name: Defect classes
concepts.summary: Particles, pattern defects, and parametric misses.
objectives: Distinguish particles, pattern defects, and parametric misses
Map a defect class onto the unit process that usually owns it

concepts.name: In-line metrology
concepts.summary: Measuring thickness, CD, and overlay before the lot is lost.
objectives: Explain measuring thickness, CD, or overlay before the lot is lost
Contrast in-line metrology with waiting for end-of-line test

concepts.name: The MOS capacitor
concepts.summary: The simplest device that still teaches the stack.
objectives: Describe the MOS capacitor as oxide plus electrode on silicon
Say what C-V on that stack teaches before a transistor exists

concepts.name: Why flatness is a lithography input
concepts.summary: Depth of focus does not forgive topography.
objectives: Explain why depth of focus cannot forgive leftover topography
Treat CMP flatness as an input to later lithography, not a cosmetic

concepts.name: Cross-contamination between tools
concepts.summary: A metal that is fine in one module poisons another.
objectives: Explain why a metal allowed in one module poisons another
Name a reason tools are segregated by material
